newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan nabs fraudsters who used PM's notepaper.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan nabs fraudsters who used PM's notepaper.

text.p: Pakistani investigators said on Tuesday they had arrested forgers who used stationery stolen from the prime minister's secretariat to issue false orders.

Rehman Malik, Assistant Director General of the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA), told a news conference that an employee at the secretariat had been arrested, along with one from the state-run Oil and Gas Development Corporation and two retired army officers, on charges of fraud and forgery.
He said the accused had forged signatures of the political secretary to the prime minister on stolen letterheads.
"They ran a parallel mini-PM-secretariat for their frauds," Malik said. "Apparently they were doing it for economic gains and did not have political motives."
Malik said his men were seeking other gang members, who had operated for the past 18 months fleecing job-seekers and businessmen of 30 to 40 million rupees ($800,000 to $1 million).
The scam was exposed after the manager of the state-owned Utility Stores Corporation received a directive telling him to procure food items from a company owned by one of the accused.
The manager wrote to the prime minister's secretariat, saying the prices quoted by the recommended firm were much higher than market rates and were therefore unacceptable.
FIA investigators then identified the fraudsters.
